news.headline: Trump offers UFC CEO Dana White White House press secretary position
news.summary: President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that he has offered the White House press secretary job to UFC chief Dana White. The post noted that White could bring several UFC fighters as assistants. The offer follows the recent departure of former press secretary Katie Zacharia. The announcement has drawn attention due to White's background in mixed‑martial‑arts promotion.

news.headline: Trump replaces chief of staff Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller after midterm losses
news.summary: President Donald Trump announced that Susie Wiles is leaving her role as White House chief of staff and that longtime adviser Stephen Miller will assume the position. The change comes days after Republicans suffered significant defeats in the midterm elections, losing control of the Senate and many House seats. The administration said the move is part of a broader re‑organization following the electoral setback.

news.headline: Alaska Senate race probes reveal alleged ballot‑confusion scheme involving Dan Sullivan and Mary Peltola
news.summary: Federal investigators sent letters to about 20 Democrats about a possible effort to recruit a candidate named Dan J. Sullivan to confuse voters in the Alaska Senate race. The race pits incumbent Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan against Democrat Mary Peltola and is extremely close under Alaska's ranked‑choice system. The DOJ inquiry and related legal challenges have drawn attention to campaign tactics and election integrity. The outcome could affect control of a Senate seat in a tightly divided chamber.

news.headline: Secret Service arrests Venezuelan migrant near White House on alleged Trump threat
news.summary: The U.S. Secret Service detained a Venezuelan migrant in Washington, D.C., after finding firearms in a stolen vehicle and hearing a threat to kill President Donald Trump. The individual was arrested near the White House and is being investigated for a possible assassination plot. The case highlights concerns about border enforcement and security around the presidential residence.

news.headline: Houston Mayor Whitmire Limits Police Cooperation with ICE After Democratic Wins
news.summary: Mayor John Whitmire signed an executive order restricting Houston police from notifying ICE about individuals arrested for non‑jailable offenses. The policy applies only to immigrants deemed a danger or wanted for serious crimes. The change follows a Democratic sweep of state elections in Texas. Officials say it reflects a new approach to local immigration enforcement.

news.headline: Podcasters Jennifer Welch and Angie Sullivan face sponsor backlash after joking about Charlie Kirk
news.summary: Left‑leaning podcasters Jennifer Welch and Angie Sullivan laughed at a social‑media post that referenced digging up and killing conservative commentator Charlie Kirk. The joke sparked outrage, leading several advertisers, including Cash App and Chewy, to cut ties with their "I've Had It" podcast. The hosts later issued apologies for the insensitive remarks. The incident highlights heightened partisan tensions surrounding political commentary and sponsor sensitivities.

news.headline: Israeli President taps Gadi Eisenkot to form new government
news.summary: President Isaac Herzog announced that opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot will be given the first opportunity to assemble a coalition government in Israel. The move follows a fragmented election where Netanyahu's bloc fell short of a majority. Eisenkot has 28 days to negotiate a governing coalition. The decision could end Benjamin Netanyahu's long tenure as prime minister.

news.headline: California Governor Newsom Commutes All Death Sentences to Life Without Parole
news.summary: Governor Gavin Newsom announced that all 548 death row inmates in California will have their sentences commuted to life without parole. The action does not repeal the state's death penalty statute, so future prosecutors could seek capital punishment in new cases. Newsom framed the move as aligning with California's values and public safety goals. The decision comes as he prepares to leave office and is speculated to be a presidential candidate.

news.headline: Gunman opens fire in Krakow market square, killing at least five
news.summary: A gunman drove a vehicle into Krakow's Main Square and opened fire on pedestrians, causing multiple casualties. Police confirmed at least five deaths and more than a dozen injuries. The suspect, a Polish citizen, was taken to hospital after being shot by police. The incident occurred in a popular tourist area, raising security concerns.

news.headline: State Department announces $20 Million reward for tips on Iran's nuclear program
news.summary: The U.S. State Department's Rewards for Justice program is offering up to $20 million for information on Iran's nuclear activities, including scientists, technology and facilities. The offer is being publicized through various channels, including Signal, Tor and social‑media tip lines. The reward comes amid ongoing concerns about Iran's nuclear capabilities and U.S. efforts to gather intelligence. President Trump has previously claimed the Iranian nuclear program was "obliterated," adding political tension to the announcement.

satire.headline: Promises Kept: Democrats Deliver On Affordability By Making Stocks Way Cheaper
satire.summary: U.S. — Democrats proudly announced that they had already delivered on their campaign promise to improve affordability, having made stock prices far, far cheaper in just a few days.

satire.headline: Dozens Come To Faith After Church Purchases Golf Simulator
satire.summary: BARTLESVILLE, OK — Dozens of local residents were welcomed into the faith this week after Cornerstone Church purchased a golf simulator.
